rules.problem: Trigger 'Breast finding' is the natural parent of every checked finding (Breast lump, Pain of breast, Maternal breastfeeding, Breast normal are all its direct children), which matches the page title and the house guidance for complaints that are not recorded common symptoms. Every red-box item and every discriminator the page uses to reach a 'likely' diagnosis is in the check_for; temperature is a routine vital. 'Which may be fluctuant' is optional on the page, so (snomed_concept "Fluctuant" "finding") is not required.

Structure (fever OR body pain) AND lump AND breast pain matches the red box. No precoordinated 'painful breast lump' concept exists, so lump + pain is the best available pair; it would also match a lump with pain elsewhere in the breast, a slight widening that the page's wording does not strictly support.

rules.rule: Diagnose probable mastitis associated with lactation
rules.problem: Overlaps with the abscess rule: a breastfeeding patient with a painful lump and fever/body pain satisfies both, so the system will output probable mastitis (clinic flucloxacillin) and probable breast abscess (urgent surgical referral) at once. The page's lower algorithm is headed 'Approach to the patient with breast symptoms not needing urgent attention', so mastitis is meant only for patients who do not meet the red box; the page's own discriminator is weak ('which may be fluctuant'). The grammar does not allow (no (active_condition ...)), so this cannot be excluded cleanly. This reproduces an ambiguity on the page rather than inventing one; it should go to a clinician. The concept is right: plain 'Mastitis' does not exist in SNOMED and the rule already requires breastfeeding.

The 'No' branch (temp < 38 AND no body pain) in a breastfeeding patient with painful breast is encoded faithfully. The page gives one combined 'Engorgement/blocked duct likely'; splitting it into two probable rules with identical evidence is a reasonable encoding. 'Milk engorgement of breast' (child of 'Engorgement of breasts associated with childbirth') fits the lactation context; 'Breast engorgement in pregnancy, the puerperium or lactation' (finding) is an equally close alternative, not a closer one.
Same evidence as the engorgement rule, as the page intends. 'Obstruction of lactiferous duct' is the closest SNOMED concept for 'blocked duct'.

The diagnosis concept 'Pain of breast' is the same concept as one of its own evidence findings, so the rule restates a recorded finding as a probable diagnosis. SNOMED has no better general concept (mastalgia is a synonym of 'Pain of breast'; 'Cyclical mastalgia' and 'Non-cyclical mastalgia' are narrower than the page). The not-breastfeeding, breast pain, exam-normal conditions are faithful to the page. Worth confirming that VHA wants a probable diagnosis that equals its evidence.

rules.rule: Urgent: breast symptoms with likely breast abscess
rules.problem: Urgent is justified by the red box heading 'Give urgent attention'. Referencing the probable abscess diagnosis via active_condition follows the house pattern for a red box that names a likely diagnosis.

summary: All 31 claims are faithful to the page: every concept exists, every number and comparison direction is right, and each diagnosis sits in the right rule at the right certainty. The most consequential problem is the inherited overlap between the mastitis and breast abscess rules: a breastfeeding patient with fever and a painful lump triggers both, although the page restricts the mastitis branch to patients not needing urgent attention and separates the two only by 'may be fluctuant'; this is a page ambiguity for a clinician, not an invention. Minor: the mastalgia rule diagnoses 'Pain of breast' from 'Pain of breast' because SNOMED has no distinct general mastalgia concept, and the single page box 'Engorgement/blocked duct likely' is split into two identical-evidence probable rules.
